content.title: 3-2-1! Everything to know about Artemis II launch in 90 seconds or less
content.text: Updated March 31, 2026, 12:39 p.m. ETArtemis II launch scheduled to take place April 1 from Florida.Catch up on what the mission is all about in about a minute.Want to watch in person or livestream? Here's how.For the first time in more than 50 years, humans will strap themselves on top of a rocket and head farther than ever before into space.The Artemis II launch this week sets several firsts but even beyond that, it's one of the first steps planned to establish a base on the moon, with a goal of later heading to Mars.If you've missed all that, here's everything to catch you up in less than 90 seconds, 60 seconds if you read fast!When is Artemis II launch date?Artemis II is scheduled to launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.When is launch time for Artemis II?As of Tuesday, March 31, the launch time currently is scheduled for no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET April 1.Artemis II countdown clockHow to watch Artemis II launch coverageThe USA TODAY Network Space Team will provide live updates at 10 a.m. April 1 at floridatoday.com/space.USA Today to livestream Artemis II launchWhere else can you watch livestream of Artemis II launch?Watch livestreams on:Amazon PrimeNASA's YouTube channelNASA+Amazon Prime membershipDoes Artemis II have a launch window?The launch is currently set for no earlier than 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026, in a two-hour launch window.Are there backup dates for Artemis II if launch doesn't happen April 1?Additional available launch times for NASA Artemis II are:7:22 p.m. April 28:00 p.m. April 38:53 p.m. April 49:40 p.m. April 510:36 p.m. April 66:06 p.m. April 30What's best place to watch Artemis II launch in Florida?Multiple parks on the Indian River in Titusville, on Florida's east coast, provide a view directly across Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral launch pads.As many as 400,000 people are expected to be on the Space Coast for the launch.➤ Tourist guide, hotel info for Artemis II launchWhere will Artemis II go?Artemis II will fly around the Earth before going around the moon inside the Orion spacecraft.The 10-day mission around the moon will send astronauts farther into space than even the Apollo missions.Where will Artemis II launch?The SLS rocket will lift off from Kennedy Space Center Launch Pad 39B at Cape Canaveral, Florida.The northernmost launch pad at Kennedy Space Center, 39B, previously was home to space shuttle and Saturn V launches.Will Artemis II land on the moon?No. Artemis II will fly around the moon.How tall is the SLS rocket used in Artemis II mission?NASA's Space Launch System rocket is 322 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty's 305 feet but still smaller than the 363-foot-tall Saturn V. It's also the most powerful rocket NASA has ever launched, with 8.8 million pounds of thrust.On top of the SLS rocket is the Orion crew capsule.Why is Artemis II flying around the moon? Moon base coming?Artemis II will be the first crewed test flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft. The crew are testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing.NASA is looking to establish a permanent foothold on the moon's south pole, using a series of crewed and uncrewed missions in the years ahead to build a moon base before possibly venturing to Mars.Who is on board Artemis II?The four astronauts selected for the Artemis II mission include:Reid Wiseman, commanderVictor Glover, pilotChristina Koch, mission specialistCanadian Space Agency's Jeremy Hansen, mission specialist3 of 4 astronauts on Artemis II set firstsThree of the four astronauts on the Artemis II mission are setting records:first woman to venture near the moon: mission specialist Christina Kochfirst Black man to venture near the moon: pilot Victor Gloverfirst Canadian to venture near the moon: mission specialist Jeremy HansenWhat's special about Artemis II?Astronauts have not traveled beyond Earth orbit since the 1972 Apollo 17 mission.Artemis II also will be about 250,000 miles in space — farther than the record-setting Apollo 13 mission.Astronauts on board also will see sights on the far side of the moon never before seen by humans.What's weather forecast for Artemis II? 80% go for launch NASA currently forecasts an "80% chance of favorable weather condition."The National Weather Service forecast for Wednesday calls for partly sunny skies with a high near 79. Winds will be out of the east at 10-15 mph, with gusts as high as 20 mph.Will Artemis II astronauts return to Florida?No. When they return to Earth, the astronauts in the Orion capsule will make a parachute-assisted water landing in the Pacific Ocean near California.Contributors: Rick Neale and Brooke Edwards, FLORIDA TODAY, and Eric Lagatta, USA TODAY NetworkCheryl McCloud is a journalist for the USA TODAY Network-Florida's service journalism Connect team.
